description: Nobody Counts the Ad Breaks — essay pairs AFTER public-source research pass 2026-09-02. Regulatory/audit facts marked checked; thesis/mechanism pairs remain novel/asserted until sealed.

pairs.source_text: What is the core gap argued in Nobody Counts the Ad Breaks?
pairs.target_text: Almost everything about how children's games manipulate has been documented, litigated, or measured — except the one number a parent needs at the moment of decision: how often *this* app stops the child during ordinary play. Regulatory, audit, census, and advocacy records exist; none resolve to one app, one child, one afternoon.
pairs.reason: README thesis + DRAFT opening; novel essay claim

pairs.source_text: What does Nobody Counts the Ad Breaks say engagement telemetry gets wrong?
pairs.target_text: Time-on-app and interaction count treat frustration and delight as the same shape. The proxy is not merely imprecise — it is inverted: a worse interruption-heavy experience can produce a better engagement number. Same failure mode as assessment proxies (worksheet for understanding).
pairs.reason: DRAFT 'The session looked great'; novel thesis

pairs.source_text: What was the Epic Games FTC settlement amount and split in December 2022?
pairs.target_text: RESEARCH-CHECKED: FTC announced Dec 19, 2022 settlements totaling $520 million — $275 million civil penalty for COPPA Rule violations (largest FTC rule penalty then claimed) and $245 million consumer redress for dark-pattern / unwanted-charge billing practices. Primary: ftc.gov press release.
pairs.reason: Draft claim corroborated 2026-09-02 via FTC primary press + secondary

pairs.source_text: What was the Cognosphere / Genshin Impact FTC outcome in January 2025?
pairs.target_text: RESEARCH-CHECKED: FTC announced ~Jan 17–18 2025 that Cognosphere (HoYoverse / Genshin Impact) agreed to pay $20 million and face order terms including blocking under-16 loot-box purchases without parental consent, addressing COPPA and deceptive loot-box cost/odds practices. Primary: ftc.gov case page and press release.
pairs.reason: Draft claim corroborated 2026-09-02 via FTC primary

pairs.source_text: What did Xiao and Park find about South Korean loot-box probability disclosure compliance?
pairs.target_text: RESEARCH-CHECKED: Acta Psychologica 2025 content analysis of the 100 highest-grossing South Korean iPhone games: 90 contained paid loot boxes; of those, 84.4% disclosed probabilities under the law mandatory from March 2024 — better than cited self-regulation comparators, still not 100%, and accessibility/prominence often poor. DOI 10.1016/j.actpsy.2025.105490.
pairs.reason: Draft figures corroborated 2026-09-02 via DOI abstract + techxplore secondary

pairs.source_text: What free machine-readable per-app sources does Nobody Counts the Ad Breaks name, and what is the F-Droid Ads caveat?
pairs.target_text: F-Droid AntiFeatures (including Ads and Tracking) and Exodus Privacy tracker reports. RESEARCH-CHECKED: F-Droid docs apply Ads to apps containing advertising and note most ad-serving apps use proprietary ad SDKs and therefore never enter the FOSS repo — so absence of Ads inside F-Droid is not a clean bill for the commercial Play population.
pairs.reason: Draft claim + F-Droid primary docs corroborated 2026-09-02

pairs.source_text: What interruption fact does Nobody Counts the Ad Breaks propose recording?
pairs.target_text: How many times, in ten minutes of ordinary play, the application stops the child to show something they did not ask for — counting interruptions (paywall, rate-us, daily reward, video ad) not ads alone; with dismissal mode (immediate / after_delay / unskippable / deceptive_close), observed version+date, and who observed. Provenance states: assumed / fitted / measured. No composite score.

pairs.source_text: What is the Playgate artifact claimed in Nobody Counts the Ad Breaks?
pairs.target_text: CLAIM BOUNDARY: Essay states apps/playgate in safe-app-store is merged, in CI, with 118 assertions including eleven mutations. Treat as operator-asserted until a dated CI/commit receipt is attached in the data room — do not auto-seal engineering metrics from the essay alone.
pairs.reason: README artifact section; firewall engineering claims

pairs.source_text: What are the claim boundaries for Nobody Counts the Ad Breaks?
pairs.target_text: Safe to claim: maps an extensive public record and names a missing per-title interruption measurement; proposes a provenance-stated field. Not a screen-time moralism, not a claim that games are bad, not a new statute proposal. Regulatory dollar figures and audit percentages must cite primary sources (FTC, DOI). Commercial ad-load vendors (Sensor Tower etc.) are named as existence of paid measurement, not as endorsed data partners.
pairs.reason: DRAFT 'What this paper is not' + research pass discipline
